newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IndMin says mulling CEZ 96 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Czech IndMin says mulling CEZ 96 dividend.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Wednesday his office was still considering whether to allow electricity generator CEZ a.s. to pay out its first-ever dividend on 1996 earnings.

CEZ's board has said it would propose to pay out at least a 30 crown dividend per share for 1996, but the final decision on the proposal lies with the state, which holds a 67 percent stake in the firm.

Dlouhy, whose ministry acts on the state's behalf at CEZ, told reporters on Wednesday that increasing costs and a delay in construction of the nuclear power plant at Temelin suggested dividends were not on the agenda.
But he added that CEZ, the second most heavily capitalised issue on the Prague Stock Exchange, needed the best possible credit rating for its financing.

"A part of a quality rating is whether the company pays dividends or not, so a certain compromise will have to be found," Dlouhy said. He declined to say whether the compromise meant a lower than proposed dividend.
CEZ recorded a 7.85 billion crown net profit in 1996, after 8.06 billion in 1995, according to Czech accounting standards.
